Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a right apical opacity (indicated by the arrow) and destruction/absence of the right second rib, which are classic radiographic signs of a Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor). In an elderly smoker, this malignancy can invade local structures like the brachial plexus or sympathetic chain, and the "disorientation episodes" may be attributed to paraneoplastic syndromes (e.g., SIADH causing hyponatremia) or metastatic disease associated with lung cancer.
